_doc: The Economic Chronicle: the player's unified ledger (systems/ledger.js), the realms' weekly economic indices (world/economyIndex.js), the gazette the player reads in market towns and their net worth (systems/economyChronicle.js), and fashions that move the nobles' and merchants' baskets (world/fashions.js). Nothing here draws RNG: fashions start on a hash of the world seed and the week.
_ledger: Every gold flow the player has, by source. A system reports a flow with Ledger.record(player, category, signed amount); the day's flows close into player.financeHistory (one row a day, the last `days` days). kind: 'op' counts in the income statement (earned or spent running your affairs), 'cap' is capital and stock (goods bought and sold, works and properties bought, loan principal: shown apart, not as profit or loss), 'memo' is paid inside a price (a guild's toll on what you sold: shown as 'of which', never summed). Trading margins (stalls, portTrade, storeRooms, forwards, caravanTrade) are each sale against the average cost of the good bought (systems/priceKnowledge.js). Categories not listed count as 'op' in the 'other' group.

fraud.name: Forgeries, false claims and false coin

guildTolls.name: Guild tolls in your sale prices

saleDuties.name: Import duties in your sale prices

bills.name: Bills of exchange drawn and paid

_netWorth: Net worth = gold + bank deposits + royal bonds + goods (packs, holds, store-rooms) at the best price your book knows the stalls pay (base x goodsShare when unknown) + book value of properties (their cost, losing propertyDepreciation a year down to propertyFloor), works (what you put in x their repair), ships (their value x shipShare) and your trading company - loans owed and rent in arrears. Sampled weekly (worthWeeks samples).
_indices: Each realm's economy, measured every `every` days over its settlements (population-weighted) and for the whole world, kept for historyWeeks samples: food = what the food goods cost against their base price (100 = base; season, scarcity and debased coin all count), goods = the same over every market good weighted by what people spend on it, trade = goods moved by merchants in a market turn, shortages = towns short of something (scarcity at least shortageAt), dearth = towns in food dearth, idle = share of hands without work, welfare = how content the people are, treasury, debt ratio and coin purity. changeWeeks: the 'since' comparison for inflation. News for the heralds: a realm's food index at least dearAt, at least dearRel times the world's and up at least surgePct since changeWeeks ago (the lean weeks alone are no news), or its goods index up inflationPct and inflationRel more than the world's (a debased coin shows here; each realm at most once per newsGapWeeks). Readers, on the realm's food against the world's: KingdomStability's target ('Cost of living': dearer than dearFrom costs perPoint a point up to stability.max, cheaper than plentyBelow gives stability.plenty) and KingdomAI.considerWar (dearer than war.dearFrom lowers a crown's confidence, at most war.max).
_gazette: Realm-level indices are public: a gazette is posted weekly in every settlement with a market. Standing in one, the player reads it: their own realm's latest numbers and the other realms' a week older (news travels), the world's, and the fashions within gazetteRadius hexes. Town-level prices stay what the price book knows (systems/priceKnowledge.js).
_fashions: Fashions at court (world/fashions.js): every `every` days, while fewer than maxActive run and from minDay, a fashion starts at a living realm's capital with startChance (a hash of the world seed and the week). It spreads outward speed hexes a day up to maxRadius, rising over `rise` days, holding `hold` days and fading over `fade` days, weaker with distance (falloff). While it holds a town, the strata listed (with their weight) want more (or less) of its goods: goods a market keeps change the town's need of them (TownLabour.demandMults), so prices move with the stock; goods no market keeps (exotics, silk, ivory) sell for more at the stalls and ports (x the same factor). Players with standing can set one (playerSet): at a capital where their reputation is at least minReputation (or a realm they rule), for prestige House Prestige and gold, halved with an artist or architect client in their pay, at most once every cooldown days; their fashion is `power` times as strong and lasts `longer` times as long.
